:::{#exm-huffman-code}
#### A Huffman code for a five-valued variable

<!-- no-figure: the example is one table of codewords and three numbers -->

Let $X$ have five values with [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) $p = (0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1)$.
The code below carries out the three steps of @def-huffman-code,
breaking ties in favor of the node listed first.
It then computes the [expected length](source-coding.qmd#def-expected-length) $L$ of the code,
the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) $\entropyf{X}$ with base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm),
and the sum $\sum_x 2^{-\ell(x)}$ of @thm-kraft-inequality.

```{r}
#| label: huffman-code
huffman_code <- function(p) {
  codewords <- rep("", length(p))
  weights <- p
  members <- as.list(seq_along(p))
  while (length(weights) > 1) {
    ord <- order(weights)
    first <- ord[1]
    second <- ord[2]
    low <- members[[first]]
    high <- members[[second]]
    codewords[low] <- paste0("0", codewords[low])
    codewords[high] <- paste0("1", codewords[high])
    merged_weight <- weights[first] + weights[second]
    merged_members <- c(low, high)
    two_smallest <- 1:2
    rest <- ord[-two_smallest]
    weights <- c(weights[rest], merged_weight)
    members <- c(members[rest], list(merged_members))
  }
  codewords
}
p <- c(0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1)
codewords <- huffman_code(p)
len <- nchar(codewords)
surprisal <- -log2(p)
expected_length <- sum(p * len)
entropy <- sum(p * surprisal)
kraft_sum <- sum(2^(-len))
data.frame(p = p, codeword = codewords, length = len)
c(expected_length = expected_length, entropy = entropy, kraft_sum = kraft_sum)
```

The code has expected length $L = `r expected_length`$ [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit)
and the source has entropy $\entropyf{X} = `r round(entropy, 3)`$ bits,
so $L - \entropyf{X} = `r round(expected_length - entropy, 3)`$ bits.
The sum $\sum_x 2^{-\ell(x)} = `r kraft_sum`$ is the largest value @thm-kraft-inequality allows,
and no codeword is the beginning of another, as @thm-huffman-prefix-code says.

:::
